title: Opening
part: PART 1 — Lite mode (what a clinician sees)
do: demo open in Lite mode, top of the page, nothing loaded yet.

cues.text: Dear Professor Al-Haddad — the demonstration you asked for.
No sound: the captions are the commentary.
First the eight-stage pipeline, then the Grad-CAM maps.

title: The two views
part: PART 1 — Lite mode (what a clinician sees)
do: point at the Lite / Full switch in the top bar, do not click it yet.

cues.text: This is Lite mode — the clinician's screen. The research view comes later.

title: Loading the patient
part: PART 1 — Lite mode (what a clinician sees)
do: drop `294_right.jpeg` into the right-eye slot, then `294_left.jpeg` into the left-eye slot.

cues.text: One patient, both eyes, uploaded as ordinary files.
EyePACS case 294 - proliferative retinopathy in both eyes.
The system is not told that grade. We compare against it.

title: The case opens
part: PART 1 — Lite mode (what a clinician sees)
do: let the two thumbnails settle; the case note appears under the slots.

cues.text: Each image is checked to be a fundus photograph, then a patient case opens on the server.

title: Entering the pipeline
part: PART 1 — Lite mode (what a clinician sees)
do: on the left-eye card, click "Show preprocessing stages".

cues.text: Every stage can now be inspected one by one, on this eye.

title: Stage 0 — original
part: PART 1 — Lite mode (what a clinician sees)
do: stop on slide "0. Original".

cues.text: The image as it left the camera: a left eye, disc on the left.

title: Stage 0 — canonical flip
part: PART 1 — Lite mode (what a clinician sees)
do: click ▸ to "0. Canonical flip". Step back and forward once so the mirroring is visible.

cues.text: Stage 0 mirrors every left eye into right-eye orientation.
After it, the optic disc sits on the same side in every image.

title: OD and fovea detection
part: PART 1 — Lite mode (what a clinician sees)
do: click ▸ to the "OD · fovea detection" slide. Show the confidence chip; toggle the probability heat map on and off; drag the fovea marker slightly, then undo the drag (do not save).

cues.text: A trained heat-map detector finds the optic disc and the fovea.
It reports its confidence and can show its probability map.
A clinician who disagrees drags the markers; the pipeline re-runs.

title: Stage 1 — rotation
part: PART 1 — Lite mode (what a clinician sees)
do: click ▸ to "1. OD-fovea rotation".

cues.text: Stage 1 rotates the disc-to-fovea axis horizontal.
Camera tilt stops being a difference between images.

title: Stage 2 — FOV crop and resize
part: PART 1 — Lite mode (what a clinician sees)
do: click ▸ to "2. FOV crop + resize".

cues.text: Stage 2 crops the field of view and resizes to 512 by 512.
The resize is isotropic — nothing is stretched.

title: Stage 3 — FOV mask
part: PART 1 — Lite mode (what a clinician sees)
do: click ▸ to "3. FOV mask".

cues.text: Stage 3 builds a binary mask of the field of view.
The mask becomes the fourth input channel of the network.

title: Stage 4 — flat-field
part: PART 1 — Lite mode (what a clinician sees)
do: click ▸ to "4. Flat-field". Step back to Stage 2 and forward again once.

cues.text: Stage 4 removes the camera's illumination gradient.
The dark corners lift; lesions stop competing with shading.

title: Stage 5 — CLAHE
part: PART 1 — Lite mode (what a clinician sees)
do: click ▸ to "5. CLAHE". Step back and forward once.

cues.text: Stage 5 is dual-constraint CLAHE on the lightness channel.
The second constraint keeps the optic disc from burning out.
These two photometric stages carry 41 % of the measured gain.

title: What the network receives
part: PART 1 — Lite mode (what a clinician sees)
do: scroll to the channel row under the CLAHE slide — R, G, B, FOV.

cues.text: The channels of the final stage are the CNN input itself.
Red, green, blue — and the field-of-view mask.

title: The two stages you cannot see here
part: PART 1 — Lite mode (what a clinician sees)
do: stay on the same screen.

cues.text: Two stages are absent by design: augmentation runs only in training,
and Stage 7 is the normalisation that produces the tensor.

title: Inference
part: PART 1 — Lite mode (what a clinician sees)
do: click "Run inference"; wait for the result card.

cues.text: The classifier: EfficientNet-B3, five grades, four channels.
Patient grade, class probabilities, referable flag, measured latency.

title: Per eye
part: PART 1 — Lite mode (what a clinician sees)
do: point at the per-eye panel.

cues.text: Each eye is graded on its own; either eye can make a patient referable.

title: Grad-CAM
part: PART 1 — Lite mode (what a clinician sees)
do: scroll to the attention overlays; let both eyes finish rendering.

cues.text: Grad-CAM, computed live from the model checkpoint, for each eye.
Attention gathers on the affected periphery, away from disc and vessels.
The line below it is generated from the map geometry.

title: The limit of that claim
part: PART 1 — Lite mode (what a clinician sees)
do: point at the note under the overlays.

cues.text: This is attention alignment, not clinical localisation of pathology.
An interpretability tool, never a diagnostic output.

title: The ophthalmologist agrees
part: PART 1 — Lite mode (what a clinician sees)
do: click "Confirm prediction"; the standing verdict replaces the buttons.

cues.text: Here the model's grade matches the dataset's, and the reviewer confirms it.
One verdict per prediction, with an undo.

title: The ophthalmologist disagrees
part: PART 1 — Lite mode (what a clinician sees)
do: click undo; then "Reject — provide correct grade", choose a different grade, click "Add to training buffer".

cues.text: A disagreement is recorded the same way, with the correct grade.
It is stored in the patient case and in a buffer for retraining.

title: What survives the session
part: PART 1 — Lite mode (what a clinician sees)
do: scroll to the relabeling buffer and the statistics panel; hover "Export JSONL" without clicking.

cues.text: The buffer exports as JSONL; the totals are read from disk, so a disagreement survives a reload.

title: Switching
part: PART 2 — Full mode (the research view)
do: click the switch to Full; the sidebar appears.

cues.text: The same page in Full mode: everything behind the demo.

title: Overview
part: PART 2 — Full mode (the research view)
do: Overview tab; scroll slowly once.

cues.text: The claim of the work: the model is preprocessing plus the network.
The pipeline is a component of it, not preparation of the data.

title: Pipeline
part: PART 2 — Full mode (the research view)
do: Model → Pipeline; scroll through the stage diagram to the end.

cues.text: All eight stages, including the two the live strip cannot show.
Stage 6 — affine, colour jitter, noise, JPEG — training time only.
Stage 7 — dataset-specific normalisation into the tensor.

title: Architecture and explainability
part: PART 2 — Full mode (the research view)
do: Model → Architecture, stop on the 4-channel stem; then Model → Explainability.

cues.text: The only change to the backbone is a fourth channel in the stem.
And this is how the attention maps are produced and scored.

title: Datasets
part: PART 2 — Full mode (the research view)
do: Datasets; scroll once.

cues.text: Eight datasets: EyePACS for training, the rest for transfer and external clinics.

title: Experiment 1
part: PART 2 — Full mode (the research view)
do: Exp 1 (H-1): Factorial; stop on the A–D table.

cues.text: Two backbones by two arms, 35,126 images, five-fold cross-validation.
Weighted F1 rises from 0.754 to 0.819 — the same on both backbones.
The arms differ in pipeline and initialisation, so the gain is the configuration's.

title: Experiment 2
part: PART 2 — Full mode (the research view)
do: Exp 2 (H-2): Ablation; stop on the cumulative chart, then the per-stage contributions.

cues.text: Experiment 2 adds the stages one at a time, under one initialisation.
Each contributes significantly; together they reproduce the whole gain.
Flat-field and CLAHE lead — that is the 41 %.

title: Experiment 4 — explainability
part: PART 2 — Full mode (the research view)
do: Exp 4 (H-5): Explainability; stop on the ALO table.

cues.text: The attention claim, measured on 54 IDRiD images with lesion masks.
Overlap rises for all four lesion types; every interval excludes zero.

title: Transfer and external clinics
part: PART 2 — Full mode (the research view)
do: Exp 3 (H-4): APTOS, then Exp 5 (H-4/H-7): Transfer.

cues.text: Zero-shot transfer to APTOS, then two external clinical sets.
Plus 6.9 points on IDRiD, plus 5.4 on Messidor-2.

title: Devices and small data
part: PART 2 — Full mode (the research view)
do: Exp 6 (H-6): Devices, then Exp 7: Small Data.

cues.text: Across five camera groups the spread between devices narrows.
On a small clinical set the pipeline still wins.

title: Results
part: PART 2 — Full mode (the research view)
do: Results → Main Metrics, then Statistical Tests.

cues.text: The headline metrics, and the tests behind them: DeLong, McNemar, Holm.

title: The cost
part: PART 2 — Full mode (the research view)
do: Validation → Computational.

cues.text: The fourth channel costs under 1 % in FLOPs and 24 megabytes.
The pipeline is a cheap prior.

title: Closing
part: PART 2 — Full mode (the research view)
do: back to Overview, then to the Lite demo screen.

cues.text: The demo is online; I will keep the backend running to suit you.
Thank you for your time and for your review.
